verdict.root_cause: cartservice latency is entirely consumed by its cart-cache round trips: every trace shows ~301-307ms of self-time in leaf HGET/HMSET spans while GetCart/AddItem handler spans contribute under 1ms, and ~600ms writes and ~900ms end-user POSTs decompose into two or three of these fixed ~300ms cache operations [tr_9f968ce8d2bc]. Operations still succeed - logs show continuous error-free cart handling through 19:38, with only inter-operation spacing stretching from single-digit ms to ~600ms [tr_5d665bee9c5a] - so this is a wait, not a failure. The near-constant penalty (300.8-307.4ms, identical on reads and writes) matches a fixed injected delay on the cache path rather than load-dependent queueing, and the change record contains repeated platform-automation fault injections on exactly that path, including traffic-shaping sidecars adding fixed egress delay on the cart-service network namespace [tr_a9cf71300764]. frontend, checkoutservice and loadgenerator alerted because they were waiting on cartservice.
verdict.reasoning: Traces localise all excess duration to cache leaf spans and explicitly rule out cartservice application logic, other downstream callees, and the frontend client layer [tr_9f968ce8d2bc]. Logs show degradation not unavailability: no errors, reconnects, startup banners or crash loop [tr_5d665bee9c5a], so the mechanism is waiting on the cache, i.e. dependency_latency. Metrics contributed nothing in either direction - the error-ratio series is empty in both incident and baseline windows, attributed to a label-set mismatch [tr_a84bc1d09e9f][tr_ffe30945fc03]. The change log supplies the best explanation for a fixed ~300ms on this exact path via automated delay injection [tr_a9cf71300764]; I treat its claim that all injections were reverted before onset as untrusted, since the trace shape is inconsistent with a clean baseline. Fix is to remove the residual delay injection on the cart cache path.
open_questions: Whether a delay-injection sidecar or tc rule was actually still active on the cart-service network namespace at onset, since the change log claims all were reverted and is marked untrusted.
When the latency shift began: logs are truncated between ~15:46 and ~19:37 and no cartservice latency metric series was retrievable.
Health of redis-cart itself (CPU, memory, saturation, restarts) was never measured, so intrinsic cache slowness is not excluded.

alternatives.root_cause: redis-cart itself became slow (saturation or its own resource pressure), adding ~300ms to every cart cache operation.
alternatives.why_not: The penalty is a uniform ~300ms across reads and writes and across all ten traces, which fits a fixed injected delay better than load-dependent queueing; no redis-cart telemetry was gathered, so this is unmeasured rather than supported.

alternatives.root_cause: A REDIS_ADDR override still pointed cartservice at an alternate cache port whose path is slower.
alternatives.why_not: A wrong endpoint would typically produce connection errors or failures, but logs show clean successful operations [tr_5d665bee9c5a], and the change record shows the override reverted 49m before onset [tr_a9cf71300764].

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is expected. The observation that would justify a later action is a cartservice latency series (or a fresh trace sample) showing the ~301-307ms per-cache-operation self-time, paired with a trusted confirmation that a delay-injection sidecar or tc qdisc is currently attached to the cart-service network namespace, or a redis-cart health reading showing intrinsic slowness. Either of those turns an unverifiable claim into a targetable one.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if someone produces evidence that a *currently active* configuration on cartservice is the delay source - i.e. an apply-type change in effect at onset, or a live tc/sidecar attachment confirmed outside the untrusted change log. It is also wrong if latency persists and nobody ever inspects redis-cart, since that unmeasured dependency is the remaining mechanism. Note that neither the fix nor its absence can be tracked in metrics today: the only cartservice metric series queried is empty in both incident and baseline windows [tr_a84bc1d09e9f, tr_ffe30945fc03], so any confirmation must come from traces or log inter-operation spacing, not dashboards.
proposal.risk: The permitted config_revert does not match the mechanism and would likely make things worse. The only cartservice configuration recorded in change history is the REDIS_ADDR override pointing the cache at an alternate port, and that override was already reverted 49 minutes before onset [tr_a9cf71300764]; restoring the 'previous configuration' risks re-applying the bad endpoint and converting a 300ms degradation into cart failures for every caller. Nothing in the change record was in effect at onset, so the action's precondition - a configuration change inside the incident window - is not met. restart_service is also unjustified: the logs show an unbroken serving process with no startup banner, reconnect, or error lines through 19:38 [tr_5d665bee9c5a], so evidence points at the network/cache path rather than process state, and a restart is marked irreversible. rollback_image is excluded because all three hotfix image updates were reverted roughly six hours before onset [tr_a9cf71300764]. scale_service is unavailable in this world.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody, since nothing changes. Had an action been taken on cartservice, the container recreate would reset connections for frontend and checkoutservice (both alerted), and loadgenerator would see the resulting request failures; those three are waiting on cartservice today and would absorb the downtime for a fix whose target is not yet established.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Four services alerting near-simultaneously across the cart/checkout/frontend path is not a single quiet warning and cannot be dismissed. Cart is a plausible shared dependency, so latency or a resource issue behind it is the cheapest starting prior.
